A Greek Orthodox wedding (Sacrament of Holy Matrimony) is a sacred, deeply symbolic ceremony divided into two main parts: the **Service of Betrothal** and the **Service of Crowning**.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX1ieIj2feyqW2WOMJUSIJlp9ey02rVBKQzgXSuWpmVlBCBXd5FWtjHRdAOr3EWlQTybRMXNyg2Y5i4-m4-AeGpq7FIHCJ1v33dYY344LorUsnASmUNRzawAGviRKEhRaMIkoqi8s-noQOCwb-IMR1PXjf5Rv14Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXgSLMxUlbCnvWpo_3I6HCkDAviuwuXd7YQJNxowIXMnDq6w8RECZIdh_7nYoggNYnq3t3edhc6uuVz6-JxgmbDtcT8DwRWIHBnbL24RlflqUZnm0pTCb9at6N7Bz2GwUsxrDRSenCmBA3NsV70UT91aqWnxzBVMIbLg)

### Key Parts of the Ceremony

- **The Processional:** The groom waits for the bride at the church entrance, hands her the bouquet, and takes her right hand after her father accompanies her down the aisle. Unlike many Western traditions, there are **no spoken vows** ; the focus is on prayer and grace.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXX7PER3rz5CzfGXlfDtXJzY994xoLmN-KAA2R-qFZSuyWBkd7s94Qk5ZUE50MHSEZpPkNGbBvFEcmpEjEAuRUxirHEOBzPndthZmgIxGhMVNJHUcEbH8zYc_-unp-CZkf-FIhFiP_6P7ypsGI)
- **Service of Betrothal (Engagement):** The priest blesses the rings and places them on the right-hand ring fingers of the couple. The **Koumbaro** or **Koumbara** (the Orthodox sponsor/best man or maid of honor) swaps the rings back and forth three times to symbolize unity in the Holy Trinity.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF1xW-0ggEQRo91XK5qphFX97UgRMU_7bcy4sHCfteGemYBMENgXcdnMTrSBeL5WAy0WLjj4eTYAEKK1_EOAWWW5noUyBkrEmCkD847-1qnhpeqUlYsxobG6PLpMaVDursdLIQp7w17022A8EZORSsXFN0r4iUc3fpaVgCqr8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX1ieIj2feyqW2WOMJUSIJlp9ey02rVBKQzgXSuWpmVlBCBXd5FWtjHRdAOr3EWlQTybRMXNyg2Y5i4-m4-AeGpq7FIHCJ1v33dYY344LorUsnASmUNRzawAGviRKEhRaMIkoqi8s-noQOCwb-IMR1PXjf5Rv14Q)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqgEBxCJF178l78PkkMmFOszDg1MtTMPlErnY36BWfN5BBkFZuaIleiOY1idU1QEThtNrnNeFKbzw5Am92HMBcjJuLfqjsyGa2IRhinYWIw5FnwrZIn-ss6e_zPtaQTDV5Owzt5aqRyEtrvb7_RWurmeuUqDSepy8Qgp7bVJSBAzBwXwk-oydeLEOXEMar-IUCdvp3ZNhf6EqmBc-V7ovOX4ePMEsSjximPNArQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXTb4D8zvS83rbGWLKLTJUj4_L2-SNk2WakvZYl99y7H-ZATdVL3vA8F1831XzhdBHPOKdx2awQg7AzU5ohylKkyw7_mcCiKBD5ti4YmQNZZ7Csa-Vq1IDFf_u-PaJ7tTo_BZTlH_Do3K5)
- **Service of Crowning (Stephanomata):** 
	- **Candles (Lambathes):** The couple holds lit white candles representing the light of Christ.
	- **Crowning:** The priest places wreaths or crowns (*stefana* ) joined by a ribbon on the heads of the bride and groom, declaring them the king and queen of their new household. The Koumbaro exchanges the crowns three times.
	- **Common Cup:** The couple shares sips of wine (usually three times each) from a common cup, symbolizing that they will share all of life's joys and burdens together.
	- **Dance of Isaiah:** Led by the priest holding the Book of Gospels, the couple takes a ceremonial threefold walk around the small table (analogion) as a joyous first steps as a married couple.
	- **Removal of Crowns:** The priest offers a final blessing and gently removes the crowns.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXTb4D8zvS83rbGWLKLTJUj4_L2-SNk2WakvZYl99y7H-ZATdVL3vA8F1831XzhdBHPOKdx2awQg7AzU5ohylKkyw7_mcCiKBD5ti4YmQNZZ7Csa-Vq1IDFf_u-PaJ7tTo_BZTlH_Do3K5)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF1xW-0ggEQRo91XK5qphFX97UgRMU_7bcy4sHCfteGemYBMENgXcdnMTrSBeL5WAy0WLjj4eTYAEKK1_EOAWWW5noUyBkrEmCkD847-1qnhpeqUlYsxobG6PLpMaVDursdLIQp7w17022A8EZORSsXFN0r4iUc3fpaVgCqr8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX1ieIj2feyqW2WOMJUSIJlp9ey02rVBKQzgXSuWpmVlBCBXd5FWtjHRdAOr3EWlQTybRMXNyg2Y5i4-m4-AeGpq7FIHCJ1v33dYY344LorUsnASmUNRzawAGviRKEhRaMIkoqi8s-noQOCwb-IMR1PXjf5Rv14Q)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXX_LPUKrxpnSV5nZ0FnwRvQBCEUijZzB1bvsb4PTggsdf8VD8IUqUxEvWEZp9fPCtteZKEbvf6jkQHmvSHKSy9SmLgfbT91XQFSo6vOe7Hsa_9vB899qvXxAvn9nygJncdiiYaAg_ac_4Y)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXur-PC04gpHRpKvGq1r7HPmuYiQ-YyJ_QUIS8stOVl08xAJicy3qd5scPfPrLmzngHKQrCz3q3_pUYRqWeJYrvZELpZRa8087s86CDpYvhKtG0xe1pnVvPvw)[[7]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqgEBxCJF178l78PkkMmFOszDg1MtTMPlErnY36BWfN5BBkFZuaIleiOY1idU1QEThtNrnNeFKbzw5Am92HMBcjJuLfqjsyGa2IRhinYWIw5FnwrZIn-ss6e_zPtaQTDV5Owzt5aqRyEtrvb7_RWurmeuUqDSepy8Qgp7bVJSBAzBwXwk-oydeLEOXEMar-IUCdvp3ZNhf6EqmBc-V7ovOX4ePMEsSjximPNArQ)

### Important Traditions

- **The Koumbaro / Koumbara:** The primary witness and spiritual sponsor who plays a central role in the exchange of rings and crowns.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF1xW-0ggEQRo91XK5qphFX97UgRMU_7bcy4sHCfteGemYBMENgXcdnMTrSBeL5WAy0WLjj4eTYAEKK1_EOAWWW5noUyBkrEmCkD847-1qnhpeqUlYsxobG6PLpMaVDursdLIQp7w17022A8EZORSsXFN0r4iUc3fpaVgCqr8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)
- **Koufeta:** Odd-numbered Jordan almonds (sugar-coated) given to guests; the indivisible odd number symbolizes endurance and an undivided life together.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)
- **No Vows / Facing the Altar:** The couple faces the altar (not each other) during the rite to signify that Christ is at the center of their union.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXgSLMxUlbCnvWpo_3I6HCkDAviuwuXd7YQJNxowIXMnDq6w8RECZIdh_7nYoggNYnq3t3edhc6uuVz6-JxgmbDtcT8DwRWIHBnbL24RlflqUZnm0pTCb9at6N7Bz2GwUsxrDRSenCmBA3NsV70UT91aqWnxzBVMIbLg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjLm2jMNwbKCTVzsJiMqMcU-_KHO7x4cfTcYh4f2JBiw7xIBQ4y8jducvAwFHZIHHg-EWuR2htdYJAfbUK-81-Ef8USQBOevigyGjaoxR2ZCJ-Q5JFaY2bM4ZXF1bYK85ZcYIUjssTWcP7dXLFquv)

For official guidelines, requirements (such as baptismal certificates and certificates of celibacy), or scheduling, you can consult the [Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX1ieIj2feyqW2WOMJUSIJlp9ey02rVBKQzgXSuWpmVlBCBXd5FWtjHRdAOr3EWlQTybRMXNyg2Y5i4-m4-AeGpq7FIHCJ1v33dYY344LorUsnASmUNRzawAGviRKEhRaMIkoqi8s-noQOCwb-IMR1PXjf5Rv14Q) or the [Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXur-PC04gpHRpKvGq1r7HPmuYiQ-YyJ_QUIS8stOVl08xAJicy3qd5scPfPrLmzngHKQrCz3q3_pUYRqWeJYrvZELpZRa8087s86CDpYvhKtG0xe1pnVvPvw).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX1ieIj2feyqW2WOMJUSIJlp9ey02rVBKQzgXSuWpmVlBCBXd5FWtjHRdAOr3EWlQTybRMXNyg2Y5i4-m4-AeGpq7FIHCJ1v33dYY344LorUsnASmUNRzawAGviRKEhRaMIkoqi8s-noQOCwb-IMR1PXjf5Rv14Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXur-PC04gpHRpKvGq1r7HPmuYiQ-YyJ_QUIS8stOVl08xAJicy3qd5scPfPrLmzngHKQrCz3q3_pUYRqWeJYrvZELpZRa8087s86CDpYvhKtG0xe1pnVvPvw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXoQtiC_VyjdHw1E_XVBPNb_AYH34tYmWUVr7Yfka5mxUW-5zc0MFl5mgwX-tJACH6dctNgSd1Qp1zDul6YlNK5K7QudzzcKlcD2-LDDbXfpYgjTjXeHR7ea_fLwMFe72kXCI-t_iRnQ)Here is a visual overview of how the Greek Orthodox crowning ceremony and traditions unfold:

items.text: The Koumbaro / Koumbara: The primary witness and spiritual sponsor who plays a central role in the exchange of rings and crowns. Koufeta: Odd-numbered Jordan almonds (sugar-coated) given to guests; the indivisible odd number symbolizes endurance and an undivided life together. No Vows / Facing the Altar: The couple faces the altar (not each other) during the rite to signify that Christ is at the center of their union.
